entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Order 
This is first bail application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for grant of regular bail relating to FIR/Crime No. 15/2023 dated 11.1.2023 registered at Police Station Kotwali, District Sehore for the offences punishable under Sections 420,
409 of the Indian Penal Code.
2. The senior counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the case.
The allegation against the applicant is that while working as erstwhile Samiti Prabandhak of a Cooperative Society, some financial irregularities on a large scale were committed by the applicant.
The amount recovered from the famers were not entered into the records of the society and was embezzled by the applicant.

It is contended by the senior counsel that on similar set of allegation, the applicant was confronted with the order of termination, which has been NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:55624 2 MCRC-44761-2024 stayed by this Court vide interim order dated 9.5.2023 passed in Writ Petition No. 10507 of 2023.
It is further submitted that the applicant is ready to deposit 40% of the defalcated amount.
It is further submitted that the applicant is aged about 59 years and is suffering from some chronic disorders.
The applicant is in custody since 23.8.2024 and trial would take considerable time to conclude, therefore, the applicant be released on bail.

sentences.text: The counsel for the State has opposed the application and submitted that total amount of defalcation exceeds an amount of Rs. 1 Crore and as per communication dated 18.11.2022 (Annexure A-4), total outstanding amount is Rs.70,83,882.17/- along with interest, which is recoverable from the applicant.
Therefore, the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail.

4. Heard the submissions and perused the case diary.
5.
On perusal of record, it reflects that the applicant is aged about 59 years and is suffering from some chronic disorders.

The applicant undertakes to deposit 40% of the defalcated amount,
therefore, considering the totality of the circumstances, this Court finds it to be a fit case to release the applicant on bail.

Therefore, without commenting on the merit of the case, the application is allowed subject to following conditions:-
6.

It is directed that the applicant shall be released on bail subject to depositing 40% of defalcated amount of Rs.70,83,882.17/- within 3 months from today and also on furnishing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for his appearance before the said Court on all such dates as may be fixed by that Court in this regard during NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:55624 3 MCRC-44761-2024 the pendency of trial.
7. It is further directed that the applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 480(3) of the Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.

8. It is made clear that if the applicant fails to deposit 40% of the defalcated amount in terms of this order within 3 months from today, this order shall cease to have its effect automatically without further reference to the Bench.

(MANINDER S. BHATTI) JUDGE PB Laxminarayan Chandrawanshi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103765817/
